category_title: Students who communicate knowledge through visual and performing arts to overcome vocabulary limitations
minimal_context: The student is using watercolors in art class to create a personal landscape representing the weather.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start using the watercolors to create your personal landscape to represent the weather.

STUDENT: (Paints on the paper) I am trying to express the weather, but the watercolor is not giving me the detail I want.

TUTOR: Just keep working on it.

STUDENT: I messed up the details. Every time I mess up something, I try again.

TUTOR: Okay, go ahead and try again.

STUDENT: (Paints over the same spot repeatedly) When I get it wrong, I try again and again. So, I never give up. But the watercolor still won't give me the detail I want for my landscape!

options.A: Ask the student to say keywords verbally and help them write these down on their watercolor landscape.
options.B: Integrate the 'TU model' processes to support decision-making, planning, and communication talents during the watercolor activity.
options.C: Use open-ended questions to guide the student in their landscape painting, offering thought-provoking questions and questions-as-suggestions.
options.D: Use a relaxing session of brainstorming ideas for the landscape, explaining that no ideas will be reproached, good or bad.
